revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: restated from what a user of the library needs
revisions.title: RFC 9562 version 7 identifiers
revisions.body: Every identifier uuid7_gen() returns shall be a 16-byte binary UUID laid out as RFC 9562 section 5.7 version 7: unix_ts_ms as a 48-bit big-endian integer in bytes 0 to 5, the version 7 in the high nibble of byte 6, 12 bits of rand_a, the variant 0b10 in the two high bits of byte 8 and 62 bits of rand_b. Identifiers shall be exchanged only in this binary form; the text form (8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal) is the caller's.
revisions.rationale: Consumers store, compare and transmit identifiers as 16 raw bytes and hand them to any RFC 9562 reader; one binary form keeps the interface free of formatting choices.
revisions.criteria: For every identifier the integration and scenario suites generate: (byte 6 & 0xF0) == 0x70 and (byte 8 & 0xC0) == 0x80; under the test clock at 0x010203040506 ms bytes 0 to 5 decode to it; review of app/uuid7.h: no text conversion in the interface.

revisions.body: The 62-bit rand_b field shall come from the 8 bytes the active RNG returns for the call: byte 8 keeps the low six bits of the first RNG byte, bytes 9 to 15 are the next seven RNG bytes unchanged.
revisions.rationale: RFC 9562 rand_b; the tail is the unguessable part of the identifier.
revisions.criteria: With a scripted RNG the scripted bytes appear in bytes 8 to 15 as specified.

revisions.title: Unpredictable bits
revisions.body: The 62 bits of rand_b of every identifier shall be taken unchanged from the entropy source active for that call.
revisions.rationale: Consumers expose identifiers (kyr_core's session and token identifiers) and rely on them being hard to guess from the ones issued before (SSAR asset A3); the timestamp and the counter in rand_a are guessable, so the unpredictability rests on rand_b alone. Identifiers are not secrets (SSAR R5).
revisions.criteria: With a scripted source the scripted bytes appear as specified: byte 8 keeps the low six bits of the first byte, bytes 9 to 15 are the next seven bytes.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: restated from what a user of the library needs
revisions.title: Timestamp is the time of issue
revisions.body: The timestamp of an identifier shall be the Unix time in milliseconds (CLOCK_REALTIME) at its generation, except that it may run up to UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS ahead of the clock to keep the order of UUID7-SRS-007 when the clock stalls or steps back or when more than 4096 identifiers are issued in one millisecond.
revisions.rationale: Consumers read the creation time back from the identifier and sort records by it; the allowance is the price of a strict order that never waits.
revisions.criteria: With the real clock and no burst the decoded timestamp lies between two CLOCK_REALTIME reads taken around the call; under the test clock a wall-clock millisecond later than the last identifier's is used as it is.

revisions.reason: TS issue 1: SRS and ICD; criticality high for SSAR asset A2 (two approvers)
revisions.title: Strict monotonicity
revisions.body: Within one process, the (timestamp, sequence) pair of every successful uuid7_gen() call shall be strictly greater than the pair of every successful call that completed before it.
revisions.rationale: Time-ordered database keys must append; the platform keys LMDB records by these identifiers.
revisions.criteria: The decoded pairs strictly increase in every single-thread and per-thread sequence the suites generate, the clock stalling or going back included.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: restated from what a user of the library needs
revisions.title: Strict order within a process
revisions.body: Within one process, every identifier uuid7_gen() returns shall compare with memcmp() greater than every identifier returned before its call began, whatever the wall clock does; when no greater identifier can be represented (the 48-bit timestamp is exhausted) uuid7_gen() shall refuse with -3 instead of issuing one.
revisions.rationale: The platform keys LMDB records by these identifiers: new records must append in byte order, and no identifier may be issued twice (SSAR asset A2).
revisions.criteria: The decoded (timestamp, rand_a) pairs strictly increase and memcmp() order equals generation order in every single-thread and per-thread sequence of the suites, across sequence rollovers, a stalled clock and a clock stepped back; a reservation at the 48-bit limit returns -3 and the next call after it is unaffected.

revisions.reason: TS issue 1: SRS and ICD; criticality high for SSAR asset A2 (two approvers)
revisions.title: Ahead-of-clock bound
revisions.body: uuid7_gen() shall refuse with -3, leaving the reservation state unchanged, any reservation whose millisecond would exceed the wall clock by more than UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS; the bound is not applied while the clock read fails.
revisions.rationale: Borrowed milliseconds must stay bounded so a burst or an abusive caller cannot date identifiers arbitrarily far in the future.
revisions.criteria: With the state parked at now + UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS and sequence 4094, one more identifier is issued, then -3 twice, then success once the clock advances 1 ms.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: restated from what a user of the library needs
revisions.title: Order across restarts
revisions.body: After uuid7_init() or uuid7_raise_floor() imports an identifier the caller persisted, every identifier the process then returns shall sort after the imported one and after every identifier the process returned before; an import older than the process's newest identifier shall change nothing.
revisions.rationale: A restarted server, a restored snapshot or a clock set back must not issue keys that sort before the ones already stored: the consumer imports its newest stored key at start (kyr_core raises the floor from its newest key after opening its database).
revisions.criteria: Identifiers generated after importing an identifier dated after the clock sort after it, through either function; importing (2000, 10) then (1000, 50) leaves the next identifier at (2000, 11); the restart scenario passes.

revisions.title: Order across restarts
revisions.body: After uuid7_init() or uuid7_raise_floor() imports an identifier the caller persisted, every identifier the process then returns shall sort after the imported one and after every identifier the process returned before; an import older than the process's newest identifier shall change nothing.
revisions.rationale: A restarted server, a restored snapshot or a clock set back must not issue keys that sort before the ones already stored: the consumer imports its newest stored key at start (kyr_core raises the floor from its newest key after opening its database).
revisions.criteria: Identifiers generated after importing an identifier dated after the clock sort after it, through either function; importing (2000, 10) then (1000, 50) leaves the next identifier at (2000, 11); the restart scenario passes.

revisions.title: Refused imports
revisions.body: uuid7_init() and uuid7_raise_floor() shall refuse an identifier to import that is not version 7 (-2), not of variant 0b10 (-3) or dated more than UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS after the wall clock (-4), and a refused import shall change nothing.
revisions.rationale: A corrupt, foreign or future-dated stored key (a poisoned import or a runaway clock) must be a loud error at start, never a generator that dates every later identifier in the future.
revisions.criteria: Each kind of invalid identifier returns its code from both functions, and the next identifier is the one the generator would have issued without the call.

revisions.title: Built-in RNG source
revisions.body: The built-in RNG shall fill the request from getrandom(2) on Linux, retrying on EINTR, and shall read the remainder from /dev/urandom when getrandom(2) fails or returns no data.
revisions.rationale: RFC 9562 6.9 asks for a cryptographically secure source; the kernel CSPRNG is one.
revisions.criteria: Inspection of _default_rng() confirms the call order, the EINTR retry and the fallback.

revisions.title: Caller-supplied entropy
revisions.body: A caller shall be able to install its own entropy source at any time, through uuid7_set_rng_func() or uuid7_init(), and to restore the built-in one with NULL; the source installed last shall serve every later identifier, also when it was installed while the first identifier was being generated.

revisions.title: Entropy before reservation

revisions.rationale: A sequence value consumed by a failed call would leave a gap and waste the 4096-entry space.
revisions.criteria: After two failed calls in one millisecond, the next successful call decodes to the sequence right after the last successful one.

revisions.title: Clock failure
revisions.body: When the wall clock cannot be read, uuid7_gen() shall keep issuing identifiers in the order of UUID7-SRS-007, their timestamps no longer advancing, and count the failure; uuid7_clock_failure_count() shall return the number of failures since the process started: 0 on a healthy clock, never decreasing.
revisions.rationale: Losing the clock must not stop a server or break its keys; the frozen timestamps are misleading, so the consumer needs a counter to alert on.
revisions.criteria: Inspection of the clock-failure path: the failed read counted and taken as 0, the ahead bound skipped, the reservation continued from the state; uuid7_clock_failure_count() returns 0 throughout the suites on a healthy clock.

revisions.body: When the wall clock cannot be read, uuid7_gen() shall keep issuing identifiers in the order of UUID7-SRS-007, their timestamps no longer advancing, and count the failure; uuid7_clock_failure_count() shall return the number of failures since the process started: 0 on a healthy clock, never decreasing.
revisions.rationale: Losing the clock must not stop a server or break its keys; the frozen timestamps are misleading, so the consumer needs a counter to alert on.
revisions.criteria: Inspection of the clock-failure path: the failed read counted and taken as 0, the ahead bound skipped, the reservation continued from the state; uuid7_clock_failure_count() returns 0 throughout the suites on a healthy clock.

revisions.title: Thread safety
revisions.body: Every function of the interface shall be callable concurrently from any number of threads; no two calls in one process shall return the same identifier, each identifier's rand_b shall come from one entropy source, and the identifiers of each thread shall keep the order of UUID7-SRS-007, entropy-source changes and floor imports racing included.
revisions.rationale: The platform's servers generate identifiers on many threads with no lock of their own and may change the entropy source while running.
revisions.criteria: 16 threads x 100000 identifiers: every thread's sequence strictly increases and all identifiers are distinct; entropy-source swaps and floor imports racing generation break neither; the concurrent scenario passes.

revisions.reason: TS issue 1: SRS and ICD; criticality high for SSAR asset A2 (two approvers)
revisions.title: Non-blocking generation
revisions.body: uuid7_gen() shall never block, sleep or wait for the wall clock; its only retry shall be the compare-and-swap of the reservation state.
revisions.rationale: Callers sit on request paths; a lock or a wait would couple them.
revisions.criteria: Analysis of uuid7_gen(): no lock, no sleep, no wait; the loop repeats only after a failed compare-and-swap (another thread reserved first, or the weak form failed spuriously), so some thread always progresses.

revisions.title: Never waits
revisions.body: uuid7_gen() shall never block, sleep, take a lock or wait for the wall clock to advance; under contention some call shall always complete.
revisions.rationale: Callers generate identifiers on request paths and inside their own critical sections: a generator that waits stalls them, one that locks can deadlock with them.
revisions.criteria: Analysis of uuid7_gen(): no lock, no sleep, no wait; the loop repeats only after a failed compare-and-swap, which means another call succeeded or the weak form failed spuriously; the same-millisecond scenario moves to the next logical millisecond without the clock advancing.

revisions.title: Burst capacity
revisions.body: The generator shall issue 4096 identifiers per logical millisecond and absorb bursts of up to 4096 x UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS identifiers ahead of the wall clock before refusing.

revisions.criteria: Analysis of the reservation rule (UUID7-SRS-010, UUID7-SRS-011): 4096 sequence values per logical millisecond, UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS + 1 milliseconds before the bound.

revisions.title: Burst capacity
revisions.body: uuid7_gen() shall issue at least 4096 identifiers per millisecond of the wall clock and absorb a burst of up to 4096 x UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS identifiers ahead of it; beyond that it shall refuse with -3, change nothing, and issue again once the clock has caught up.
revisions.rationale: Consumers insert in bulk (imports, migrations) faster than the clock advances: they need a known capacity and a refusal they can back off from, never a stall or a silent loss of order. With the default bound the burst is 40,960,000 identifiers.
revisions.criteria: Under the test clock 4096 identifiers take one logical millisecond and the next one the following millisecond; at the bound uuid7_gen() returns -3 with the state unchanged and succeeds again after the clock advances; analysis of the reservation rule gives the burst size.

revisions.title: Static state
revisions.body: The library's mutable state shall be static and fixed: one 64-bit reservation word, one callback pointer and one 64-bit failure counter, all atomic (24 bytes on x86-64).
revisions.rationale: A fixed footprint needs no initialisation, no teardown and no allocation.
revisions.criteria: nm on the release object lists exactly these three data objects, 8 bytes each, in .bss.

revisions.title: No allocation, no held resources
revisions.body: The library shall not allocate memory and shall hold no file descriptor between calls: a descriptor it opens to read entropy shall be opened close-on-exec and closed before the call returns.
revisions.rationale: The caller owns every buffer, and a server that forks or executes children must not leak descriptors it does not know of.

revisions.reason: SVS: the analyses, inspections, reviews and pipeline gates
revisions.title: Burst capacity
revisions.body: Analysis of the reservation rule: 4096 sequence values per logical millisecond; a reservation is refused only beyond now + UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS.
revisions.criteria: With the clock frozen, 4096 x (UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS + 1) identifiers are issued before the first refusal, 40,960,000 of them ahead of the wall clock with the default bound.

revisions.reason: SVS and SUITP: the test cases of tests/ (written by ecss/make.sh)
revisions.title: Abuse bound: generation refuses to run more than UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS ahead of the wall clock.
revisions.body: With the wall clock frozen, the generator may borrow logical milliseconds only up to UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS past it. Park the state exactly at the bound (sequence one short of exhaustion), prove the last in-bound id is minted, then prove the next reservation — which would need bound+1 — is refused with -3 and leaves the state untouched. Advancing the wall clock by one millisecond lifts the bound by one and the refused reservation succeeds.
revisions.criteria: Every assertion of test_gen_refuses_beyond_ahead_bound holds.

revisions.reason: Change request raised
revisions.title: Rework the requirements from the consumer's needs and record the design trade-offs (on the owner's instruction)
revisions.body: Rework the technical specification of uuid7 from what a user of the library needs: the interface contract, the RFC 9562 format, ordering and uniqueness, burst capacity, thread safety, failure behaviour (entropy source, clock), no allocation, the technical budgets (time per identifier, stack, static data, code size), portability, build and packaging. Few requirements, each testable, each with its rationale, verification method and acceptance criteria; the ICD items as interface artifacts. Keep an identifier when its intent survives; supersede or make obsolete the others through the lifecycle, each superseded item linked to its superseder. Record the design trade-offs as decisions, rationales and assumptions linked to the requirements they answer and the components they shape. Relink the verification cases, retag the code and the tests, and hold a delta qualification review that freezes baseline QR-2.
revisions.rationale: The owner, 2026-10-10: the 66 requirements were reverse-engineered from the code and many restate how it works instead of what a user of the library needs; the design trade-offs are to be kept. The owner allowed the project to adjust the requirements on the owner's behalf in the rms.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: an ICD item as an interface
revisions.title: Constants
revisions.body: uuid7.h defines two unsigned integer constants: UUID7_SIZE_BYTES, the size of an identifier, 16 bytes; and UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS, how far in milliseconds the timestamps may run ahead of the wall clock, 10000 unless the library is built with -DUUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS=<ms>. The bound is fixed into the library when it is built: defining the macro in a consumer changes only that consumer's view of the constant.
revisions.rationale: Callers size their buffers and their back-off from the header, not from numbers copied out of a document.
revisions.criteria: test_public_constants: UUID7_SIZE_BYTES == 16 and UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS == 10000 in the default build.

revisions.title: uuid7_gen()
revisions.body: int uuid7_gen(void* out_buf) writes one identifier, exactly UUID7_SIZE_BYTES bytes, to out_buf and returns 0; or writes nothing and returns -1 (out_buf is NULL), -2 (the entropy source failed) or -3 (the ahead bound or the 48-bit timestamp range refuses).
revisions.rationale: The one call every consumer makes.
revisions.criteria: The integration suite produces every return value: 0, -1, -2 and -3, each with the buffer checked.

revisions.title: uuid7_init()
revisions.body: int uuid7_init(uuid7_rng_function_t fn, const void* last_gen_uuid7) installs fn (NULL: the built-in source), then, when last_gen_uuid7 is not NULL, imports it as the floor; it returns 0, -2 (not version 7), -3 (not variant 0b10) or -4 (dated beyond the ahead bound). A refused import leaves the source installed and the state unchanged.
revisions.rationale: Start-up in one call: the entropy source and the newest stored identifier.
revisions.criteria: The integration suite produces every return value and checks that the source is installed before the import is validated.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: One atomic word holds the order
revisions.body:
The order state is one 64-bit word, the millisecond shifted left by 12 bits or-ed with the sequence, reserved by compare-and-swap; no lock.

Alternatives considered: A lock around a (millisecond, sequence) pair (SDD <4.7>).

Consequences: uuid7_gen() never blocks and some caller always completes; under contention callers retry the compare-and-swap (tests/stress measures the cost with ten threads); the word holds 52 bits of milliseconds, so the 48-bit range of the identifier is checked apart (V7_MS_LIMIT); the order is one per process.
revisions.rationale: Every caller races on one question, which pair is next, and one atomic word answers it without a lock a consumer's own lock could deadlock with (app/uuid7.c, g_v7_state).

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: The 12-bit rand_a is a counter
revisions.body:
rand_a carries a counter that restarts at 0 in each new millisecond (RFC 9562 6.2, method 1: a fixed-length dedicated counter); rand_b alone is random.

Alternatives considered: The other methods of RFC 9562 6.2: rand_a random, with no order inside a millisecond, or a monotonic random increment.

Consequences: Identifiers of one millisecond sort by issue and 4096 fit in one millisecond; each identifier carries 62 random bits instead of 74; the counter tells how many identifiers the process issued earlier in that millisecond, so rand_a is guessable and the unpredictability rests on rand_b.
revisions.rationale: Order inside a millisecond by construction, with the fewest moving parts (the requirement it replaces, UUID7-SRS-004, cited RFC 9562 6.2 method 1).

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Borrow the next millisecond instead of waiting
revisions.body:
When the counter of the current logical millisecond is exhausted, or the wall clock stalls or steps back, the generator continues from its own state (the next sequence value, or the next logical millisecond at sequence 0) instead of waiting for the clock.

Alternatives considered: Waiting for the wall clock to advance, which the comment of uuid7_gen() names as what the design avoids.

Consequences: uuid7_gen() never waits; timestamps can run ahead of the clock, which UUID7-DEC-004 bounds; after the clock steps back the timestamps stay at the last reserved millisecond until the clock passes it again.
revisions.rationale: Callers generate on request paths: a stall of up to a millisecond per 4096 identifiers, or an unbounded one when the clock steps back, costs them more than a timestamp a few milliseconds ahead.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Bound the run-ahead at UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS
revisions.body:
The logical clock may run at most UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS (10 s by default) ahead of the wall clock: uuid7_gen() refuses beyond it (-3) and the imports refuse a floor dated beyond it (-4), the state untouched; the check is skipped while the clock cannot be read.

Alternatives considered: No bound, as before version 1.1.0 (commit 2ff1214): an abusive caller or a poisoned floor could date every later identifier arbitrarily far in the future, and at the 48-bit limit the encoded timestamp would wrap.

revisions.rationale: See UUID7-RAT-001 for the value.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: One generator per process, in static state
revisions.body:
The generator's state is process-wide static data, three atomics, with no handle or context passed by the caller.

Alternatives considered: A generator object the caller allocates and passes to every call.

Consequences: Nothing to set up and nothing allocated; all identifiers of a process share one order, and a process cannot keep two independent orders; the tests reset the state through a seam compiled into test builds only (UUID7-DEC-013).
revisions.rationale: The order the consumers need is the process's (one key space per database), and a foundation library allocates nothing.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Built-in entropy installed on first use
revisions.body:
When no source was installed, the first uuid7_gen() installs the built-in source by a compare-and-swap from NULL, so a source installed concurrently is never overwritten.

Alternatives considered: Requiring uuid7_init() before the first identifier; a plain store of the built-in source, which a racing uuid7_set_rng_func() could lose to.

Consequences: Initialisation is optional; one atomic load more per call; the lost installation race is a path the tests cannot reach, verified by analysis (UUID7-AN-012).
revisions.rationale: app/uuid7.c, _ensure_rng_func(): a concurrent explicit call to uuid7_set_rng_func() cannot be overwritten by a racy fallback store from uuid7_gen().

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: getrandom(2) first, /dev/urandom as the fallback
revisions.body:
The built-in source reads getrandom(2) on Linux, retrying on EINTR, and reads what it could not get from /dev/urandom, opened close-on-exec and closed on every path; elsewhere it reads /dev/urandom only.

Alternatives considered: /dev/urandom alone, the first implementation (May 2026): a descriptor opened and closed for every identifier.

Consequences: On Linux the normal path opens no descriptor and holds nothing between calls; one system call per identifier, outside the time budget of UUID7-SRS-040; the fallback is slower and runs only when getrandom(2) fails; the library keeps no generator state of its own to seed.
revisions.rationale: app/uuid7.c, _default_rng(): prefer getrandom(2) so that the default path avoids file descriptors on Linux.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Survive a clock failure and count it
revisions.body:
A failed clock_gettime() reads as 0: the reservation continues from the state, the ahead bound is skipped for that call, and the failure is counted for uuid7_clock_failure_count().

Alternatives considered: The behaviour before version 0.1.0: zero timestamps without any trace; a log call, which a foundation library cannot make (commit 3d3d4d0: a counter, not a log call).

Consequences: A server keeps issuing unique, ordered identifiers without a clock; their timestamps stop advancing, which is misleading, so the count is exposed for the operator to alert on; the path is out of the test seams' reach and verified by inspection (UUID7-IN-002).
revisions.rationale: Losing the clock must neither stop generation nor pass silently (commit 3d3d4d0).

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Raise-only import of the newest stored identifier
revisions.body:
The order across restarts comes from the consumer's newest stored identifier, imported as a floor that can only raise the state; uuid7_raise_floor() imports it without touching the entropy source.

Alternatives considered: Importing at uuid7_init() only, as before version 0.1.0 (commit 3d3d4d0); the library keeping its own state in a file, which a library without I/O cannot do.

Consequences: No file and no I/O in the library; the order across restarts holds only if the consumer imports its newest key (UUID7-ASM-002); an older import never rewinds the state; a consumer that opens its database after choosing the entropy source imports later through uuid7_raise_floor().
revisions.rationale: Callers choose the entropy source early but learn their newest stored identifier only after opening their database (commit 3d3d4d0).

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Negative return codes, per function
revisions.body:
Each function returns 0 or a negative code of its own; nothing goes through errno, a log, a thread-local flag or abort().

Alternatives considered: A thread-local error flag of the built-in source (removed in May 2026, commit 557b4db); errno.

Consequences: The library depends on nothing to report; callers must check every return; the codes are per function, so -3 means a variant mismatch from uuid7_init() but a bound refusal from uuid7_gen().
revisions.rationale: Callers decide what a failure means; a library never takes the process down.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Test seams in test builds only
revisions.body:
The deterministic clock, the forced entropy failure and the state reset are compiled only with -DUUID7_TESTING, declared in app/uuid7_test.h; the integration suites link libraries built with them, apart from the delivered ones.

Alternatives considered: Testing the delivered library through its interface only, where clock stalls, steps back and the bounds cannot be produced on demand.

Consequences: Deterministic tests of the clock behaviour, the bounds and the entropy failure; the suites test a build that differs from the delivered one by the seams, and the delivered binaries carry none (UUID7-AN-004); the clock-failure path and the entropy fallback stay out of the seams' reach and are verified by inspection.
revisions.rationale: The order and the bounds depend on the clock: they are tested only if the clock can be driven.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: Versioned exports gated against a committed ABI
revisions.body:
libuuid7.so exports exactly the five functions as <name>@@UUID7_<major> (utils/uuid7.map); abi/layout.txt is the committed public ABI, and the pipeline's abi stages refuse a change without the version bump it needs.

Alternatives considered: An unversioned export list, before version 1.1.3 (commit bb824e6).

Consequences: Consumers linked against one major keep working across its minor releases; any change to a committed line needs a new major; no internal symbol can leak into the exports.
revisions.rationale: Consumers pin exact versions; the soname and the symbol versions must say what an upgrade means.

revisions.reason: UUID7-CR-004: a design trade-off recorded
revisions.title: One position-independent object, two packages
revisions.body:
One -fPIC object feeds both libuuid7.a and libuuid7.so; the runtime package libuuid7 carries the shared object, libuuid7-dev the header, the archive and the linker symlink; both build byte for byte reproducibly.

Alternatives considered: Separate objects for the archive and the shared library (before commit eb792bc); one uuid7 package (before version 1.1.2, commit 7853bf4).

Consequences: The static and the shared library hold the same code, which the integration matrix tests in both linkages; static consumers get position-independent code; a runtime-only installation carries no header.
revisions.rationale: One build of the code, delivered the way the platform's packages are.

revisions.rationale: State in UUID7-IF-002 that the callback runs on the caller's stack inside uuid7_gen() and that its frame comes on top of the budget of UUID7-SRS-053.

revisions.reason: Accepted: UUID7-IF-002 states it

revisions.reason: RID raised
revisions.title: The counter reveals the issue rate
revisions.body: With rand_a a counter, two identifiers of one millisecond show how many identifiers the process issued between them; a consumer that uses identifiers as session or token identifiers discloses its rate.
revisions.rationale: State it as a consequence of UUID7-DEC-002 and keep the unpredictability on rand_b.

revisions.reason: RID raised
revisions.title: Coverage targets leave the TS
revisions.body: UUID7-SRS-090 is made obsolete, so the coverage targets of 80 % of statements and 65 % of decisions lose their place in the technical specification, and UUID7-AN-006 verifies no requirement any more.
revisions.rationale: Keep the targets as a requirement, or name where they live now.
